agree.reason: It's a calm, believable captain's comment, but it sounds like many they've heard before, and nothing in it gives commissioners who trust their staff a reason to drop the staff's recommendation.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the claim that every boat will go out of business, and the $29,000 figure is a fair rounding of $28,800, though 'I never got all the way back' goes past the data, which stops two years after 2016.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 2016 revenue loss but misses easy strong forms: the 19% drop in bookings, the 59% of customers who'd book less, and the risk to the 70% of this season already booked.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the 2016 drop and partial recovery accurately, but the 9%-versus-80% point ignores that the cut also applies to private boats, and it never addresses the stock at 78% of target if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: The 'review after one season' request names no number, data source or consequence, and it leaves out the trip logs and reporting-app pilot the captain could commit to.

objections.reason: Saying 'not here to argue with the science' doesn't answer the staff's 78% figure, the commitments that would answer the 'just anecdote' objection are missing, and the 9% argument invites the reply that everyone has to share the cut.

fit.reason: At about 280 words it fits a two-minute spoken comment, though it leaves [NAME] and [HARBOR] blank even though the captain gave his name.
